description.value: A cross-sectional study examining the effects of schizophrenia diagnosis and overweight/obesity on gray matter volume using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry, and testing whether bilateral insula gray matter mediates the association between BMI and negative symptoms in schizophrenia.

spans.text: The whole-brain voxel-based morphometry was applied to examine the GMV alterations, and a 2 × 2 full factorial analysis of variance was performed to identify the main effects of diagnosis (SZ vs HC), BMI (NW vs OWB) factors, and their interactions.

description.value: Cross-sectional observational study of 250 Chinese Uyghur participants stratified by schizophrenia diagnosis and BMI category; no intervention or longitudinal follow-up was reported.

spans.text: There were significant main effects of diagnosis in the right hippocampus, bilateral insula, rectus, median cingulate/paracingulate gyri and thalamus, with reduced GMV in patients with SZ relative to HC (  p   < 0.001, FWE corrected) (Fig.  1 A and Table  2 ).

definition.value: Main effect of diagnosis in VBM analysis; SZ < HC.

spans.text: There were significant main effects of diagnosis in the right hippocampus, bilateral insula, rectus, median cingulate/paracingulate gyri and thalamus, with reduced GMV in patients with SZ relative to HC (  p   < 0.001, FWE corrected) (Fig.  1 A and Table  2 ).

At the secondary level of analysis, we applied a whole-brain voxel-wise general linear model with a 2 (diagnosis: SZ vs HC) × 2 (BMI category: OWB vs NW) full factorial ANOVA, controlling for age, sex, education and total intracranial volume (ICV), to determine the main effects of diagnosis and BMI factors, as well as their interaction effects.

In total, 250 Chinese Uyghur participants were included into this study, including 69 SZ patients with overweight or obesity (SZ-OWB), 74 SZ patients with normal weight (SZ-NW), 54 healthy controls with OWB (HC-OWB), and 53 healthy controls with NW (HC-NW).

value: Segmentation into gray matter, white matter, and cerebrospinal fluid

spans.text: the main steps include: a) discarded the images with visible artifacts; b) format conversion and corrected the image origin (reorientation); c) bias field correction; d) structural images were segmented into three tissue components: gray matter (GM), white matter (WM), and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF); e) the segmented images of all subjects were normalized to the Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) space using the DARTEL deformations (resliced into 1.5mm ); f) the resulting GM images ( modulated GMV) were smoothed using an isotropic Gaussian kernel of 8 mm FWHM.
